items.title: Positive coroot pairings of a dominant integral weight
items.statement: Let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$ be a dominant integral weight and let $\beta\in\Phi^+$. Then $\langle\lambda+\rho,\beta^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$; in particular $\lambda+\rho$ is regular, so the stabilizer of $\lambda+\rho$ in $W$ is trivial and $w\circ\lambda=w'\circ\lambda$ implies $w=w'$. Moreover the pairing is $W$-invariant: for all $w\in W$, $\langle w(\lambda+\rho),(w\beta)^\vee\rangle=\langle\lambda+\rho,\beta^\vee\rangle$, and $\langle w\circ\lambda+\rho,(w\beta)^\vee\rangle=\langle\lambda+\rho,\beta^\vee\rangle$. Finally every positive coroot is a nonnegative integral combination of the simple coroots, so integrality and positivity are read off on simple coroots and extended by $W$-invariance.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 3.1, pp. 9-10 and Sec. 5.3, p. 36
J. E. Humphreys, Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory, Sec. 13 (root systems), via the finite-Weyl conventions item

items.title: Bruhat covers are right multiplication by positive-root reflections
items.statement: Let $x,y\in W$ with $y\lhd x$ a cover. Then there is a unique positive root $\beta\in\Phi^+$ with $x=y s_\beta$, and $\ell(x)=\ell(y)+1$. Conversely, if $\beta\in\Phi^+$ and $\ell(y s_\beta)=\ell(y)+1$, then $y s_\beta\rhd y$ is a cover. In the notation of the Bruhat graph the label $\beta$ of the arrow $x\to y$ is characterised by $s_\beta=y^{-1}x$, and it is also the unique positive root $\gamma$ with $y=x s_\gamma$ and $\ell(x s_\gamma)=\ell(x)-1$. The proof uses the standard sign criterion $\ell(ws_\gamma)<\ell(w)\iff w\gamma<0$ together with the reflection-chain description of Bruhat order.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 3.1, p. 9 (chain description of Bruhat order)
Hemelsoet-Voorhaar, A computer algorithm for the BGG resolution, arXiv:1911.00871, Sec. 2.2, pp. 4-5

items.title: The Bruhat graph and the BGG Verma sum in degree k
items.statement: Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$, positive system $\Phi^+$, simple roots $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r$, Weyl group $W$ and $\rho$. Let $\Lambda^+$ be the dominant integral weights and let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$. Write $w\circ\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$ for the dot action. The Bruhat graph has vertex set $W$; an arrow $x\to y$ means that $y\lhd x$ is a cover in Bruhat order, i.e. $y<x$ and $\ell(x)=\ell(y)+1$. Equivalently, by [[lem-bruhat-covers-are-reflection-covers]], $x=y s_\beta$ for a unique $\beta\in\Phi^+$. A square is a quadruple $(x,m_1,m_2,y)$ with $x\rhd m_1$, $x\rhd m_2$, $m_1\rhd y$, $m_2\rhd y$ and $m_1\ne m_2$. For $0\le k\le|\Phi^+|$ put $C_k(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\ell(w)=k}M(w\circ\lambda)$, the direct sum of Verma modules over the elements of $W$ of length $k$; each $C_k(\lambda)$ is an object of $\mathcal O$ ([[def-bgg-category-o]]) with a fixed direct-sum decomposition. The endpoints are $C_0(\lambda)=M(\lambda)$ and $C_{|\Phi^+|}(\lambda)=M(w_0\circ\lambda)$, where $w_0\in W$ is the longest element; $C_k=0$ for $k>|\Phi^+|$. Because $\lambda+\rho$ is regular ([[lem-positive-root-pairings-of-a-dominant-integral-weight]]), the weights $w\circ\lambda$ are pairwise distinct, so no two distinct summands are equal as labelled modules.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions (Columbia senior thesis, 2021), Part I Sec. 3.1-3.2, pp. 9-11 (printed pp. 9-11)
A. Rocha-Caridi, Splitting criteria ... BGG resolution, Trans. AMS 262 (1980), Sec. 10, p. 353

items.title: Dominant integral dot translates embed canonically in the Verma module
items.statement: Let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$ and $w,w'\in W$. Then $w\circ\lambda\uparrow\lambda$ in the strong linkage order, so $M(w\circ\lambda)$ embeds in $M(\lambda)$; the image is the submodule generated by the (unique up to scalar) singular vector of weight $w\circ\lambda$ in $M(\lambda)$. If $w\ge w'$ in Bruhat order, then $M(w\circ\lambda)\subseteq M(w'\circ\lambda)\subseteq M(\lambda)$, and the inclusion is the unique-up-to-scalar nonzero element of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(w\circ\lambda),M(w'\circ\lambda))\cong\mathbb C$.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 3.1-3.2, pp. 9-11
A. Rocha-Caridi, Splitting criteria ..., Sec. 10, pp. 353-354; Sec. 2, Theorem 2.12

items.title: Bruhat covers give canonical Verma embeddings, and composites are inclusions
items.statement: Let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$. For every arrow $x\to y$ of the Bruhat graph (a cover $x\rhd y$) the inclusion $\iota_{x\to y}\colon M(x\circ\lambda)\hookrightarrow M(y\circ\lambda)$ of [[lem-dominant-integral-dot-translates-embed-in-the-verma-module]] is the unique-up-to-scalar nonzero $\mathfrak g$-homomorphism between these two Verma modules, and it is injective with image a proper submodule. If $x\rhd m\rhd y$ and $x\rhd m'\rhd y$ are two saturated paths, then the composites $\iota_{m\to y}\circ\iota_{x\to m}$ and $\iota_{m'\to y}\circ\iota_{x\to m'}$ are equal as maps $M(x\circ\lambda)\to M(y\circ\lambda)$: both are the inclusion of the canonical submodule $M(x\circ\lambda)\subseteq M(y\circ\lambda)\subseteq M(\lambda)$. In particular the system of inclusions is path-independent, and $\iota_{y\to z}\circ\iota_{x\to y}=\iota_{x\to z}$ whenever $x\rhd y\rhd z$ and $x>z$ (length gap two).

references.title: A. Rocha-Caridi, Splitting criteria ..., Sec. 10, p. 353 (choice of injections and induced maps $i_{ww'}$)
Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 3.2, p. 10

items.title: Bruhat intervals of rank two are diamonds
items.statement: Let $x,y\in W$ with $y<x$ and $\ell(x)=\ell(y)+2$. Then the interval $\{m:y<m<x\}$ has exactly two elements $m_1\ne m_2$; each satisfies $x\rhd m_i\rhd y$. Equivalently, the number of saturated chains $x\rhd m\rhd y$ is exactly $2$, and $[y,x]=\{y,m_1,m_2,x\}$.

references.title: Hemelsoet-Voorhaar, A computer algorithm for the BGG resolution, arXiv:1911.00871, Prop. 2.2 and Lemma 2.4, pp. 3-4 (attributed to [BGG75])
A. Rocha-Caridi, Splitting criteria ..., Definition 10.3 and the first paragraph of the proof of Lemma 10.4, p. 354
Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Lemma (10.3,10.4), p. 10

items.title: Type of a module with a Verma filtration
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (def-axiom-of-choice). For $M\in\mathcal O$ a Verma filtration is a finite increasing filtration $0=M_0\subseteq M_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq M_n=M$ by $\mathfrak g$-submodules together with weights $\psi_1,\dots,\psi_n$ such that $M_j/M_{j-1}\cong M(\psi_j)$. If such a filtration exists one says that $M$ is Verma-filtered and writes $\operatorname{Typ}M=\{\psi_1,\dots,\psi_n\}$, a finite set with multiplicity; the multiset is independent of the filtration because the Grothendieck group of the block has the standard classes as a basis ([[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]]) and characters of distinct Verma modules are linearly independent. Any finite direct sum of Verma modules is Verma-filtered with the evident type, and Verma-filteredness is preserved by tensoring with a finite-dimensional module ([[prop-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-category-o]]).

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 4.2.2 (Definition of type), p. 22
P. Etingof, Representations of Lie Groups (18.757), Corollary 20.5(i) and Exercise 20.6, pp. 101-102

items.title: Induced modules from finite-dimensional B-modules have type their weights
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $N$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak b$-module which is $\mathfrak h$-semisimple, with weight multiset $\operatorname{Wt}N$. Then the induced module $U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}N$ is Verma-filtered with $\operatorname{Typ}\bigl(U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}N\bigr)=\operatorname{Wt}N$.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 5.1, Lemma 9.5 and Fact 9.3, pp. 29-30
Van Ekeren, Topics in representation theory (IMPA 2024), Sec. 29, pp. 122-123 (the complex $U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}\Lambda^n(\mathfrak g/\mathfrak b)$)

items.title: Tensoring a Verma module by a finite-dimensional module shifts the type
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (def-axiom-of-choice). Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module with weight multiset $\operatorname{Wt}V$ and let $\psi$ be a weight. Then $M(\psi)\otimes V$ is Verma-filtered with $\operatorname{Typ}(M(\psi)\otimes V)=\psi+\operatorname{Wt}V=\{\psi+\mu:\mu\in\operatorname{Wt}V\}$. Proof route: order a weight basis $v_1,\dots,v_n$ of $V$ so that weights decrease; the $U(\mathfrak n^-)$-submodules $N_k$ generated by $v_\psi\otimes v_1,\dots,v_\psi\otimes v_k$ form a filtration with successive quotients $M(\psi+\lambda_k)$: each quotient is generated by a singular vector because $\mathfrak n^+(v_\psi\otimes v_k)\subseteq v_\psi\otimes\operatorname{span}(v_1,\dots,v_{k-1})$, and the PBW model $M(\psi)\cong U(\mathfrak n^-)$ shows the graded pieces are free of rank one.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 5.1, Lemma 9.10, pp. 31-33
P. Etingof, Representations of Lie Groups (18.757), Corollary 20.5(i), p. 101

items.title: Central-character cuts of a typed module are typed by the matching weights
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (def-axiom-of-choice). Let $M\in\mathcal O$ be Verma-filtered with type $\operatorname{Typ}M$, and for a central character $\chi$ let $M_\chi$ be the generalised central-character component ([[def-generalized-central-character-subcategory-of-o]]). Then $M_\chi$ is Verma-filtered and $\operatorname{Typ}M_\chi=\{\psi\in\operatorname{Typ}M:\chi_\psi=\chi\}$, where $\chi_\psi$ is the central character of $M(\psi)$. In particular, by the Harish-Chandra theorem in the form [[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]], $\operatorname{Typ}M_\chi$ consists of the elements of $\operatorname{Typ}M$ in the dot-Weyl orbit defining $\chi$. Proof: the projection functor is exact and kills a Verma factor unless its central character matches.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 5.1, Lemma 9.7, p. 31
Category-O supplier page: generalized central character decomposition

items.title: Weight subsets with equal root sums are unique
items.statement: Let $w\in W$ and put $\Pi_w=\{\alpha\in\Phi^+:w^{-1}\alpha\in\Phi^-\}$. Then $\#\Pi_w=\ell(w)$, $w\circ0=-\sum_{\alpha\in\Pi_w}\alpha$, and for $\rho$ the half-sum of positive roots $\rho-w\rho=\sum_{\alpha\in\Pi_w}\alpha$. If $S\subseteq\Phi^+$ satisfies $\sum_{\alpha\in S}\alpha=\sum_{\alpha\in\Pi_w}\alpha$, then $S=\Pi_w$.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 5.2, Lemma 9.6 and Fact 9.8, pp. 33-34
A. Rocha-Caridi, Splitting criteria ..., Sec. 2, Lemma 2.10-2.11 and the length formula, pp. 340-342

items.title: The standard induced resolution of the trivial module
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$, the positive system $\Phi^+$ and $\mathfrak n^-$ as in [[thm-triangular-decomposition-from-a-chosen-positive-root-system]]. The quotient $\mathfrak g/\mathfrak b$ is a $\mathfrak b$-module for the adjoint action; $\mathfrak h$ acts with weights $\Phi^-$. Projection along $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak n^-\oplus\mathfrak b$ identifies this quotient with $\mathfrak n^-$ as an $\mathfrak h$-module; its $\mathfrak b$-action is $b\cdot x=\operatorname{pr}_{\mathfrak n^-}[b,x]$, which need not vanish for $b\in\mathfrak n^+$. For $k\ge0$ put

$$B_k:=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}\Lambda^k(\mathfrak g/\mathfrak b),$$

the $k$-th exterior power being taken over $\mathbb C$ with the induced $\mathfrak b$-action. Thus $B_0=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}\mathbb C\cong M(0)$, the Verma module of highest weight $0$ of [[def-verma-module]]. By [[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]] one has $U(\mathfrak g)\cong U(\mathfrak n^-)\otimes U(\mathfrak b)$ as vector spaces, so

$$B_k\cong U(\mathfrak n^-)\otimes_{\mathbb C}\Lambda^k(\mathfrak n^-)$$

as $U(\mathfrak n^-)$-modules; hence $B_k$ is a free $U(\mathfrak n^-)$-module with $\binom{|\Phi^+|}{k}$ generators, and $B_k=0$ for $k>|\Phi^+|$. Each $B_k$ is a finitely generated $\mathfrak g$-module in the category $\mathcal O$ of [[def-bgg-category-o]]: it is generated by the image of the finite-dimensional space $\Lambda^k(\mathfrak g/\mathfrak b)$, it is $\mathfrak h$-semisimple: a root-vector exterior basis has the finite multiset of weights $\mu_S=\sum_{\beta\in S}\beta$ for subsets $S\subseteq\Phi^-$ with $\#S=k$, with distinct subsets counted separately even when their sums coincide. For $k=0$ the empty subset has weight $0$. PBW negative-root monomials shift these weights by elements of $-Q^+$, so the weights of $B_k$ lie in the finite union $\bigcup_{S\subseteq\Phi^-,\,\#S=k}(\mu_S-Q^+)$, with finite-dimensional weight spaces by PBW. Raising a fixed weight by positive roots can reach only finitely many weights in that union: their simple-root coefficients are bounded above by the finitely many $\mu$ and below by the starting weight. Hence the $U(\mathfrak n^+)$-orbit of each weight vector is finite-dimensional, proving local finiteness.

For $k\ge1$ define the differential $d_k\colon B_k\to B_{k-1}$ on elementary tensors by

$$d_k(u\otimes\xi_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\xi_k)=\sum_{i=1}^{k}(-1)^{i+1}u\xi_i\otimes\xi_1\wedge\cdots\widehat{\xi_i}\cdots\wedge\xi_k+\sum_{1\le i<j\le k}(-1)^{i+j}u\otimes\overline{[\xi_i,\xi_j]}\wedge\xi_1\wedge\cdots\widehat{\xi_i}\cdots\widehat{\xi_j}\cdots\wedge\xi_k,$$

where $\xi_i\in\mathfrak g$ are representatives of elements of $\mathfrak g/\mathfrak b$ and the bar denotes the class in $\mathfrak g/\mathfrak b$. The balanced well-definedness, $\mathfrak g$-linearity and square-zero identity are proved explicitly in [[thm-standard-induced-resolution-is-exact]]; the formula uses the actual quotient adjoint action above. Finally the counit $\varepsilon\colon U(\mathfrak g)\to\mathbb C$ induces a well-defined map $d_0\colon B_0\to\mathbb C$, $u\otimes1\mapsto\varepsilon(u)$, because $\varepsilon(u b)=0$ for $b\in\mathfrak b$ and $\varepsilon(1)=1$; it is the augmentation of the complex $(B_\bullet,d_\bullet)$, a chain complex in the sense of [[def-chain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]].

references.title: Van Ekeren, Topics in representation theory (IMPA 2024), Sec. 29, pp. 122-123 (definition and well-definedness of $D_\bullet$)
Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 5, Theorem 9.1, p. 29

items.title: The standard induced complex is a resolution of the trivial module
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The complex of [[def-standard-induced-resolution-of-the-trivial-module]] is exact in positive degrees, so $0\to B_{|\Phi^+|}\to\cdots\to B_1\to B_0\to\mathbb C\to0$ is a resolution of the trivial $\mathfrak g$-module.

references.title: Van Ekeren, Topics in representation theory (IMPA 2024), Sec. 29, pp. 122-123 (exactness in the split case)
Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 5, Theorem 9.1, p. 29 (exactness stated; standard proof)

items.title: Compatible signs exist on the Bruhat graph
items.statement: There is a function $\varepsilon$ from the set of arrows $x\to y$ of the Bruhat graph to $\{\pm1\}$ such that for every square $(x,m_1,m_2,y)$ the product of the four signs is $-1$: $\varepsilon(x,m_1)\varepsilon(m_1,y)\varepsilon(x,m_2)\varepsilon(m_2,y)=-1$. Consequently the two saturated paths of a rank-two interval always carry opposite total signs.

references.title: A. Rocha-Caridi, Splitting criteria ..., Lemma 10.4 and its proof, pp. 354-355
Hemelsoet-Voorhaar, A computer algorithm for the BGG resolution, arXiv:1911.00871, Sec. 4.2, pp. 8-9
Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Lemma (10.3,10.4) and footnote 11, p. 10 and p. 17

items.title: The BGG differential from signed Verma maps
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (def-axiom-of-choice). Fix $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$ and a compatible sign function $\varepsilon$ as in [[lem-compatible-signs-exist-on-the-bruhat-graph]]. For $k\ge1$ define $d_k\colon C_k(\lambda)\to C_{k-1}(\lambda)$ by requiring that on the summand $M(w\circ\lambda)$ of $C_k(\lambda)$ with $\ell(w)=k$ the component into the summand $M(w'\circ\lambda)$ of $C_{k-1}(\lambda)$ is $\varepsilon(w,w')\,\iota_{w\to w'}$ when $w\rhd w'$, and is $0$ otherwise; all other components are zero. Because the $\iota_{w\to w'}$ are $\mathfrak g$-homomorphisms between finitely many summands and all but finitely many components vanish, $d_k$ is a well-defined $\mathfrak g$-homomorphism of objects of $\mathcal O$; it is a degree-$(-1)$ map of graded objects with $C_k=0$ outside $0\le k\le|\Phi^+|$. Set $d_0=\pi\colon C_0(\lambda)=M(\lambda)\twoheadrightarrow L(\lambda)$, the canonical surjection of [[thm-verma-module-has-a-unique-simple-quotient]]. The maps $d_k$ are the differentials of the BGG complex; they depend on the chosen sign function only through the identity of the resulting complex up to isomorphism.

references.title: A. Rocha-Caridi, Splitting criteria ..., Sec. 10, p. 355 (definition of $d_k$ and $\eta$)
Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 3.2, p. 11

items.title: The BGG differential squares to zero
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (def-axiom-of-choice). With the maps $d_k$ of [[def-bgg-differential-from-signed-verma-maps]], $d_{k-1}\circ d_k=0$ for all $k\ge2$; with $d_0$ included the augmented sequence is a complex of $\mathfrak g$-modules $0\to C_{|\Phi^+|}\to\cdots\to C_1\to C_0\to L(\lambda)\to0$. Proof: compute the $(w_1,w_4)$-component for $w_1\in W_k$, $w_4\in W_{k-2}$. It is the sum over $w_2\in W_{k-1}$ of $\varepsilon(w_1,w_2)\varepsilon(w_2,w_4)$ times the composite of inclusions along $w_1\rhd w_2\rhd w_4$. If no such $w_2$ exists the entry is $0$. If such $w_2$ exists, [[lem-bruhat-rank-two-intervals-are-diamonds]] says there are exactly two, and by [[lem-bruhat-covers-give-unique-verma-embeddings]] the two composites are the same inclusion $M(w_1\circ\lambda)\hookrightarrow M(w_4\circ\lambda)$; the two coefficients are $\varepsilon(w_1,m_1)\varepsilon(m_1,w_4)$ and $\varepsilon(w_1,m_2)\varepsilon(m_2,w_4)$, which are opposite by the square condition of [[lem-compatible-signs-exist-on-the-bruhat-graph]]. Hence the entry vanishes. The case $k=1$ (component into $L(\lambda)$) vanishes because $\pi$ kills the images of the inclusions $M(s_i\circ\lambda)\subseteq M(\lambda)=\ker\pi$.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 4.1 Step 1, p. 14
Hemelsoet-Voorhaar, A computer algorithm for the BGG resolution, arXiv:1911.00871, Sec. 2.2 (solving $d^2=0$ square-wise), pp. 4-5

items.title: The augmentation kernel is the sum of the simple-reflection Verma submodules
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (def-axiom-of-choice). Let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$ and let $d_1\colon \bigoplus_{i}M(s_i\circ\lambda)\to M(\lambda)$ be the first BGG differential. Then $\operatorname{im} d_1=\sum_i M(s_i\circ\lambda)=\ker\pi$, where $\pi\colon M(\lambda)\twoheadrightarrow L(\lambda)$ is the canonical surjection and $M(s_i\circ\lambda)\subseteq M(\lambda)$ is the canonical submodule generated by the singular vector $f_i^{\langle\lambda,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle+1}v_\lambda$ of [[lem-simple-root-singular-vector-in-a-verma-module]]. Consequently the augmented complex is exact at $C_0$ and $L(\lambda)=\operatorname{coker}(d_1)$. Proof route (Zhou's expansion of BGG): the quotient $M(\lambda)/\sum_i M(s_i\circ\lambda)$ is finite-dimensional because $M(\lambda)\cong U(\mathfrak n^-)$ ([[thm-pbw-model-of-a-verma-module]]) and the PBW filtration identifies the quotient with a quotient of $U(\mathfrak n^-)$ by the two-sided ideal generated by the powers $f_i^{\langle\lambda,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle+1}$, whose symbol ideal contains all monomials of too large $f_i$-degree; the quotient is a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module with a unique highest weight vector of weight $\lambda$ ([[lem-a-proper-verma-submodule-misses-the-highest-weight-line]]), so complete reducibility ([[cor-every-finite-dimensional-representation-is-a-direct-sum-of-highest-weight-modules]]) and the classification [[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]] identify it with $L(\lambda)$.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 4.1 Step 2, pp. 15-17 (K8.27, K8.28a, K8.28b)
A. Rocha-Caridi, Splitting criteria ..., Sec. 10, Lemma 10.1, p. 353

items.title: Weak BGG resolution of the trivial module
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $B_k$ be the standard induced complex of [[def-standard-induced-resolution-of-the-trivial-module]] and let $B_k^{\chi_0}$ denote its generalised central-character component at the central character $\chi_0$ of $M(0)$. Then $0\to B_{|\Phi^+|}^{\chi_0}\to\cdots\to B_1^{\chi_0}\to B_0^{\chi_0}\to\mathbb C\to0$ is a resolution of the trivial module by objects of $\mathcal O$, and $\operatorname{Typ}B_k^{\chi_0}=\{w\circ0:\ell(w)=k\}$, each weight occurring once.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 5.2, pp. 33-34
Van Ekeren, Topics in representation theory (IMPA 2024), Sec. 29, pp. 123-124

items.title: Weak BGG resolution
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$ and let $\Pi_\lambda=L(\lambda)$ be the finite-dimensional simple module of highest weight $\lambda$. Put $B_k(\lambda)=\bigl(B_k^{\chi_0}\otimes\Pi_\lambda\bigr)^{\chi_\lambda}$, where $B_k^{\chi_0}$ is the base-case complex of [[lem-weak-bgg-base-case-for-the-trivial-module]] and $\chi_\lambda$ is the central character of $M(\lambda)$, the tensor product being over $\mathbb C$ with diagonal $\mathfrak g$-action and the superscript denoting the generalised central-character component of $\chi_\lambda$. Then

$$0\to B_{|\Phi^+|}(\lambda)\to\cdots\to B_1(\lambda)\to B_0(\lambda)\to\Pi_\lambda\to0$$

is a resolution of $\Pi_\lambda$ by objects of $\mathcal O$, and $\operatorname{Typ}B_k(\lambda)=\{w\circ\lambda:\ell(w)=k\}$, each weight occurring once.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 5.3, pp. 35-36
A. Rocha-Caridi, Splitting criteria ..., Introduction p. 335 and Sec. 7 (BGG Theorem 9.9)
Van Ekeren, Topics in representation theory (IMPA 2024), Sec. 29, pp. 122-124

items.title: Surjectivity modulo n-minus for free weight-generated modules (BGG 10.5)
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (def-axiom-of-choice). Let $M,N\in\mathcal O$, suppose $M$ is free as a $U(\mathfrak n^-)$-module with generators $v_1,\dots,v_n$ that are weight vectors, and let $\varphi\colon M\to N$ be a $U(\mathfrak n^-)$-module map. Then $\varphi$ is surjective if and only if the induced map $\bar\varphi\colon M/\mathfrak n^-M\to N/\mathfrak n^-N$ is surjective. Proof route: one direction is immediate; for the other, show by downward induction on the weight order that every weight vector of $N$ lies in $\operatorname{im}\varphi$. Since $N\in\mathcal O$ its weights lie in a finite union of cones $\lambda_i-Q^+$; for a weight $\mu$, write the class $\bar u$ of $u\in N_\mu$ as $\sum c_i\bar\varphi(v_i)$, which forces $\operatorname{wt}\varphi(v_i)=\mu$ whenever $c_i\ne0$; then $u-\sum c_i\varphi(v_i)\in N_\mu\cap\mathfrak n^-N=\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}f_\alpha N_{\mu+\alpha}$ lies in a sum of strictly higher weight spaces, which are contained in $\operatorname{im}\varphi$ by the induction hypothesis and the fact that $\operatorname{im}\varphi$ is a $U(\mathfrak n^-)$-submodule.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 4.2.1 (BGG Lemma 10.5), pp. 18-20
A. Rocha-Caridi, Splitting criteria ..., Sec. 7 (Prop. 7.1), pp. 345-348

items.title: Jordan-Holder factors of Verma modules dominate the head (BGG 8.12)
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$ and $w\in W$. If a simple module $L(\mu)$ occurs in a composition series of $M(w\circ\lambda)$, then $\mu=u\circ\lambda$ for some $u\ge w$ in Bruhat order; moreover $L(w\circ\lambda)$ occurs exactly once. Consequently every composition factor of $M(w\circ\lambda)$ has length at least $\ell(w)$.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 4.2.2, Theorem 8.12, p. 22
P. Etingof, Representations of Lie Groups (18.757), Theorem 20.13, p. 104 (BGG theorem on composition factors)

items.title: Composition factors of the BGG kernel lie above the degree (BGG 10.6a)
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (def-axiom-of-choice). Let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$ and let $d_k\colon C_k(\lambda)\to C_{k-1}(\lambda)$ be the BGG differential. If a simple module $L(\mu)$ occurs in a composition series of $\ker d_k$, then $\mu=u\circ\lambda$ with $\ell(u)\ge k+1$. Equivalently, no composition factor of $\ker d_k$ has the form $L(u\circ\lambda)$ with $\ell(u)\le k$. Proof route: $\operatorname{JH}C_i=\bigsqcup_{\ell(w)=i}\operatorname{JH}M(w\circ\lambda)$, and by the weak BGG resolution ([[thm-weak-bgg-resolution]]) the exact modules $B_i$ satisfy $\operatorname{JH}B_i=\operatorname{JH}C_i$; comparing the exact complex $B_\bullet$ with the partially exact complex $C_\bullet$ inductively, using additivity of Jordan-Holder factors on exact sequences, gives $\operatorname{JH}\ker d_k=\operatorname{JH}d^{B}_{k+1}(B_{k+1})\subseteq\operatorname{JH}B_{k+1}=\bigsqcup_{\ell(w)=k+1}\operatorname{JH}M(w\circ\lambda)$, and each such factor has length at least $k+1$ by [[lem-jordan-holder-factors-of-verma-modules-lie-above-the-head]].

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 4.2.2 (BGG Lemma 10.6a), pp. 22-25
A. Rocha-Caridi, Splitting criteria ..., Sec. 9 and Sec. 10, pp. 349-354

items.title: Nonzero highest-weight images survive modulo n-minus (BGG 10.6b)
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$, let $w_0\in W$, and let $M\in\mathcal O$ be an object all of whose composition factors are of the form $L(u\circ\lambda)$ with $\ell(u)\ge\ell(w_0)$. If $\varphi\colon M(w_0\circ\lambda)\to M$ is a $\mathfrak g$-homomorphism with $\varphi(v)\ne0$, where $v$ is a highest weight vector of $M(w_0\circ\lambda)$, then $\varphi(v)\notin\mathfrak n^-M$; equivalently the class of $\varphi(v)$ in $M/\mathfrak n^-M$ is nonzero.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 4.2.2 (BGG Lemma 10.6b), pp. 25-26
A. Rocha-Caridi, Splitting criteria ..., Sec. 8 (Lemma 8.1), pp. 348-349

items.title: The BGG differential induces an injection into kernel coinvariants (BGG 10.6)
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (def-axiom-of-choice). Let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$ and let $d_{k+1}\colon C_{k+1}(\lambda)\to C_k(\lambda)$ be the BGG differential. Then the induced map $\bar d_{k+1}\colon C_{k+1}(\lambda)/\mathfrak n^-C_{k+1}(\lambda)\to\ker d_k/\mathfrak n^-\ker d_k$ is injective. Proof route: $C_{k+1}=\bigoplus_{\ell(w)=k+1}U(\mathfrak n^-)v_w$ is free with weight-vector generators $v_w$, so $C_{k+1}/\mathfrak n^-C_{k+1}$ has basis the classes $\bar v_w$ of distinct weights $w\circ\lambda$; since $\bar d_{k+1}$ commutes with $\mathfrak h$, it suffices to show $\bar d_{k+1}(\bar v_w)\ne0$ for every $w\in W_{k+1}$. This is [[lem-nonzero-highest-weight-images-survive-modulo-n-minus]] applied to $M=\ker d_k$, whose composition factors have length at least $k+1$ by [[lem-kernel-generators-for-the-weak-bgg-complex]], using that $d_{k+1}(v_w)\ne0$ because it is a sum of nonzero inclusions into the summands $M(w'\circ\lambda)$ with $w\rhd w'$.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 4.2.2, pp. 22-24

items.title: Verma-filtered objects are acyclic for n-minus coinvariants
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (def-axiom-of-choice). Let $M\in\mathcal O$ be Verma-filtered. Then $\operatorname{Tor}_j^{U(\mathfrak n^-)}\bigl(\mathbb C,M\bigr)=0$ for all $j>0$. In particular the coinvariant functor $M\mapsto M/\mathfrak n^-M=\mathbb C\otimes_{U(\mathfrak n^-)}M$ is exact on Verma-filtered objects. Proof route: $M(\psi)\cong U(\mathfrak n^-)$ as $U(\mathfrak n^-)$-module ([[thm-pbw-model-of-a-verma-module]]) is free, hence $\operatorname{Tor}_j(\mathbb C,M(\psi))=0$ for $j>0$; induct on the length of a Verma filtration using the long exact Tor sequence in the second variable ([[thm-long-exact-tor-sequence-in-the-left-module-variable]]) attached to $0\to M_{i-1}\to M_i\to M_i/M_{i-1}\to0$.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 4.2.3 (the Tor computation), pp. 27-29

items.title: Tor with the trivial module is computed by the weak BGG resolution
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$ and let $B_\bullet(\lambda)$ be the weak BGG resolution of [[thm-weak-bgg-resolution]], with $\Pi_\lambda=L(\lambda)$. Then for every $k\ge1$ the induced differential $B_k(\lambda)/\mathfrak n^-B_k(\lambda)\to B_{k-1}(\lambda)/\mathfrak n^-B_{k-1}(\lambda)$ is zero, $\operatorname{Wt}\bigl(B_k(\lambda)/\mathfrak n^-B_k(\lambda)\bigr)=\{w\circ\lambda:\ell(w)=k\}$ with each weight occurring once, and consequently

$$\operatorname{Tor}_k^{U(\mathfrak n^-)}\bigl(\mathbb C,\Pi_\lambda\bigr)\cong B_k(\lambda)/\mathfrak n^-B_k(\lambda)\cong\mathbb C^{|W_k|},$$

where $W_k=\{w\in W:\ell(w)=k\}$. This is the dimension statement used by BGG in the form needed here.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 5.4 (Bott's theorem) and Sec. 4.2.3, pp. 27-29 and 37
A. Rocha-Caridi, Splitting criteria ..., Sec. 7, pp. 345-348

items.title: Dimension of the kernel modulo n-minus equals the next term (BGG 10.7)
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (def-axiom-of-choice). Let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$ and let $d_k\colon C_k(\lambda)\to C_{k-1}(\lambda)$ be the BGG differential. Then $\ker d_k/\mathfrak n^-\ker d_k$ is finite-dimensional and $\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker d_k/\mathfrak n^-\ker d_k=\dim_{\mathbb C}C_{k+1}(\lambda)/\mathfrak n^-C_{k+1}(\lambda)=|W_{k+1}|$. Proof route: $C_{k+1}/\mathfrak n^-C_{k+1}\cong\mathbb C^{|W_{k+1}|}$; $\ker d_k\subseteq C_k$ is an object of $\mathcal O$ (a submodule of a finite-length object) and is finitely generated over $U(\mathfrak n^-)$, so $\ker d_k/\mathfrak n^-\ker d_k$ is finite-dimensional; extending the partially exact complex $C_{k+1}\to C_k\to\dots\to C_0\to\Pi_\lambda$ by free $U(\mathfrak n^-)$-modules and using [[lem-surjectivity-modulo-n-minus-for-free-weight-generated-modules]] and right-exactness of $\otimes_{U(\mathfrak n^-)}$ shows $\ker d_k/\mathfrak n^-\ker d_k\cong\operatorname{Tor}_{k+1}^{U(\mathfrak n^-)}(\mathbb C,\Pi_\lambda)$; the dimension then equals $|W_{k+1}|$ by [[lem-tor-with-the-trivial-module-is-computed-by-the-weak-bgg-resolution]].

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 4.2.3 (BGG Lemma 10.7), pp. 26-29
A. Rocha-Caridi, Splitting criteria ..., Sec. 10, Lemma 10.5 and Corollary 10.6, pp. 354-356

items.title: The BGG resolution of a finite-dimensional simple module
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (def-axiom-of-choice). Let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$. The BGG complex $C_\bullet(\lambda)$ with differentials $d_k$ is a resolution of $L(\lambda)$ by Verma modules: $0\to C_{|\Phi^+|}(\lambda)\to\cdots\to C_1(\lambda)\to C_0(\lambda)\to L(\lambda)\to0$ is exact. Equivalently, $\operatorname{coker}d_1=L(\lambda)$ and $\operatorname{im}d_{k+1}=\ker d_k$ for all $k\ge1$. Proof route: the sequence is a complex by [[prop-the-bgg-differential-squares-to-zero]] and is exact at $C_0$ by [[lem-the-bgg-augmentation-has-image-the-simple-module]]. Induct on $k$: assume exactness at $C_0,\dots,C_{k-1}$. By [[lem-dimension-of-the-kernel-modulo-n-minus-equals-the-next-term]] the two finite-dimensional spaces $C_{k+1}/\mathfrak n^-C_{k+1}$ and $\ker d_k/\mathfrak n^-\ker d_k$ have equal dimension, and by [[lem-n-minus-coinvariants-map-injectively-into-the-kernel-of-the-differential]] the induced map $\bar d_{k+1}$ is injective, hence an isomorphism; then [[lem-surjectivity-modulo-n-minus-for-free-weight-generated-modules]] applied to $C_{k+1}$ (free over $U(\mathfrak n^-)$ with weight-vector generators) and $\ker d_k$ shows $d_{k+1}$ maps $C_{k+1}$ onto $\ker d_k$.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 3.2 and Sec. 4.1 (Theorem BGG and its proof), pp. 11 and 14-18
A. Rocha-Caridi, Splitting criteria ..., Sec. 10, Corollary 10.6, pp. 355-356
Hemelsoet-Voorhaar, A computer algorithm for the BGG resolution, arXiv:1911.00871, Theorem 2.5 and 2.6, p. 5

items.title: The Euler-character identity for a finite-dimensional simple module
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (def-axiom-of-choice). Let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$. In the Grothendieck group of the linkage block of $\lambda$ ([[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]], [[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]]) the finite alternating sum of Verma classes equals the class of the simple module: $[L(\lambda)]=\sum_{w\in W}(-1)^{\ell(w)}[M(w\circ\lambda)]$. Equivalently, applying the character homomorphism and the Verma character $\operatorname{ch}M(\mu)=e^{\mu}\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}(1-e^{-\alpha})^{-1}$ ([[prop-formal-character-of-a-verma-module]]), $\operatorname{ch}L(\lambda)=\sum_{w\in W}(-1)^{\ell(w)}e^{w\circ\lambda}\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}(1-e^{-\alpha})^{-1}$, the Weyl numerator identity in the form needed by the Weyl character formula. Proof: an exact finite complex has vanishing alternating sum of classes.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 3.3, pp. 11-13
P. Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras II (18.755), Sec. 26.1 and Sec. 26.3 (Weyl character formula, Theorem 26.4), pp. 139-142

items.title: The BGG resolution has length the number of positive roots
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$ and let $w_0\in W$ be the longest element. Then $\ell(w_0)=|\Phi^+|$ and $|\{w\in W:\ell(w)=|\Phi^+|\}|=1$, the BGG complex $C_\bullet(\lambda)$ is concentrated in degrees $0\le k\le|\Phi^+|$, the top term is $C_{|\Phi^+|}(\lambda)=M(w_0\circ\lambda)\ne0$, and all higher terms vanish. Consequently the resolution has length $|\Phi^+|$ and the last nonzero degree of the complex is $|\Phi^+|$; in particular the alternating sum of [[cor-bgg-euler-character-identity]] is finite and has $|W|$ terms.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 3.2, p. 11 ($\ell(w_0)=|\Phi^+|=\dim\mathfrak n^-$)
Hemelsoet-Voorhaar, A computer algorithm for the BGG resolution, arXiv:1911.00871, Sec. 2.1, p. 3

items.title: The BGG resolution for sl2
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (def-axiom-of-choice). Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2$ with $W=\{1,s\}$, positive root $\alpha$, $\rho=\alpha/2$ and $\lambda=m\omega$ with $m\ge0$ dominant integral. Then $s\circ\lambda=-\lambda-2\rho=-(m+2)\omega$ and the BGG resolution of [[thm-bgg-resolution-of-a-finite-dimensional-simple-module]] reads $0\to M(-(m+2)\omega)\to M(m\omega)\to L(m\omega)\to0$, with the injection the canonical embedding of the Verma submodule generated by the singular vector $f^{m+1}v_\lambda$ and the surjection the canonical projection. Both end degrees computed: $|\Phi^+|=1$, $w_0=s$, $C_0=M(\lambda)$, $C_1=M(s\circ\lambda)$. Verification: exactness at $C_1$ is injectivity of a nonzero Verma map, and exactness at $C_0$ is [[lem-the-bgg-augmentation-has-image-the-simple-module]]; the middle quotient $M(m\omega)/M(-(m+2)\omega)\cong L(m\omega)$ is the standard finite-dimensional quotient of dimension $m+1$.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 3.2, p. 11 (rank-one case)
P. Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras II (18.755), Sec. 25 and Sec. 25.4, pp. 134-138 (Verma modules and U(n-) model)

items.title: The A2 BGG resolution with six Verma summands
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (def-axiom-of-choice). Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_3$ with simple roots $\alpha_1,\alpha_2$, $W=S_3=\{e,s_1,s_2,s_1s_2,s_2s_1,w_0\}$, and let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$ be dominant integral. The BGG complex has $C_0=M(\lambda)$, $C_1=M(s_1\circ\lambda)\oplus M(s_2\circ\lambda)$, $C_2=M(s_1s_2\circ\lambda)\oplus M(s_2s_1\circ\lambda)$, $C_3=M(w_0\circ\lambda)$, with $d_1$ given by the two embeddings $M(s_i\circ\lambda)\hookrightarrow M(\lambda)$, $d_2$ given by the four cover embeddings ($s_1s_2\rhd s_1$, $s_1s_2\rhd s_2$, $s_2s_1\rhd s_2$, $s_2s_1\rhd s_1$) with compatible signs, and $d_3$ given by the two cover embeddings $w_0\rhd s_1s_2$ and $w_0\rhd s_2s_1$ with compatible signs. All Bruhat intervals of rank two are diamonds, so $d^2=0$ holds by the square condition; the complex is exact by [[thm-bgg-resolution-of-a-finite-dimensional-simple-module]]. Weights: $w\circ\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$ are pairwise distinct and the listed embeddings are the canonical submodules inside $M(\lambda)$.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 3.2 and Sec. 4.1, pp. 11 and 14
Hemelsoet-Voorhaar, A computer algorithm for the BGG resolution, arXiv:1911.00871, Sec. 2.2 (A2 diagram and signs), pp. 4-6

items.title: Sign cancellation in an A2 Bruhat diamond
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (def-axiom-of-choice). In the A2 setting of [[ex-the-a2-bgg-resolution-with-six-verma-summands]], the interval $[e,s_1s_2]$ has exactly two saturated paths $s_1s_2\rhd s_1\rhd e$ and $s_1s_2\rhd s_2\rhd e$, and the interval $[s_1,w_0]$ has exactly two saturated paths $w_0\rhd s_1s_2\rhd s_1$ and $w_0\rhd s_2s_1\rhd s_1$. In each case the two composites of canonical inclusions $M(x\circ\lambda)\to M(y\circ\lambda)$ coincide, while the two products of signs are opposite, so the corresponding entry of $d^2$ vanishes: for the $(w_0,s_1)$-entry of $d_2d_1$ on the weight $s_1$ one computes $\varepsilon(w_0,s_1s_2)\varepsilon(s_1s_2,s_1)+\varepsilon(w_0,s_2s_1)\varepsilon(s_2s_1,s_1)=0$. This makes the cancellation mechanism of [[prop-the-bgg-differential-squares-to-zero]] explicit on the smallest non-abelian diamond.

references.title: Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 4.1 Step 1, p. 14
Hemelsoet-Voorhaar, A computer algorithm for the BGG resolution, arXiv:1911.00871, Sec. 2.2 and Sec. 4.2, pp. 4-6 and 8-9

items.title: Unsigned Bruhat edge sums need not square to zero
items.statement: With every sign taken to be $+1$, the differential $d_k^{\mathrm{uns}}(x)=\sum_{w'\lhd w}\iota_{w\to w'}$ of the A2 complex satisfies $d^{\mathrm{uns}}_1d^{\mathrm{uns}}_2\ne0$: the $(w_0,e)$-entry of $d_1d_2$ is the sum of the four composites along $w_0\rhd s_1s_2\rhd s_1\rhd e$, $w_0\rhd s_1s_2\rhd s_2\rhd e$, $w_0\rhd s_2s_1\rhd s_2\rhd e$, $w_0\rhd s_2s_1\rhd s_1\rhd e$, and each composite is the common inclusion $\iota_{w_0\to e}$ by path-independence inside the fixed ambient $M(\lambda)$, so the entry equals $4\,\iota_{w_0\to e}\ne0$. Hence the unsigned sums do not form a complex, and the sign function of [[lem-compatible-signs-exist-on-the-bruhat-graph]] is structural, not cosmetic. (The statement is a direct two-path computation in the A2 Bruhat graph; no dependency may cite this counterexample.)

references.title: Direct computation in the A2 Bruhat graph, using the exactly-two-middles lemma (this row is ai-generated; no dependency may cite it)

items.title: The BGG complex cannot be used unchanged at a singular weight
items.statement: Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2$ and $\lambda=-\rho=-\omega$. Then $\lambda+\rho=0$ is fixed by $W$, so $w\circ\lambda=\lambda$ for every $w\in W$ and the dot-translates repeat. The 'complex' with $C_k=\bigoplus_{\ell(w)=k}M(w\circ\lambda)$ and signed inclusion maps is a complex (its square condition still holds formally), but it is not a resolution of $L(\lambda)$: since $\lambda$ is antidominant, $M(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ is simple ([[cor-antidominant-verma-modules-are-simple]]), so exactness at $C_0$ would require $d_1=0$; however every map $M(\lambda)\to M(\lambda)$ is a multiple of the identity by [[thm-verma-homomorphism-spaces-have-dimension-at-most-one]] and the differential is a nonzero signed sum of such maps, so $\operatorname{im}d_1=M(\lambda)\ne0=\ker(d_0)$. Thus $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$ (equivalently $\lambda+\rho$ having trivial stabiliser, which holds automatically for dominant integral $\lambda$) cannot be dropped; the counterexample protects the dominance hypothesis.

references.title: A. Rocha-Caridi, Splitting criteria ..., Sec. 10, p. 353 (the hypothesis $\lambda\in P^+$ in the construction)
Fan Zhou, The classical and the functorial BGG resolutions, Part I Sec. 3.2, p. 11 (requires $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$)
